terms.gloss: a wedding, the marriage ceremony and feast
evidence: Ter. And. 47: nōn sunt vērae nūptiae
terms.comment: Always plural. nūptiās facere, hold a wedding (Plaut. Aul. 2.4.9, Lewis & Short); nūptiās apparāre, get it ready (Ter. Ph. 701). The wedding day is diēs nūptiārum and anything belonging to it nūptiālis, as nūptiāle dōnum, a wedding present (Traupman 405).

phrases.latin: Quās crēdis esse hās nōn sunt vērae nūptiae.
phrases.english: This wedding you think is going on is not a real one.

phrases.latin: Spatium quidem tandem apparandīs nūptiīs, vocandī, sacrificandī dabitur paululum.
phrases.english: Surely a little time will be given for getting the wedding ready, sending the invitations and offering the sacrifice.

nuptiae.html: From nūbō, nūpsī, nūptum, which Lewis & Short marks long; the participle and its derivatives keep the vowel of the verb (nūpta).

sources: Lewis & Short: nuptiae · Lewis & Short: nuptialis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 405.
